slides.title: Deadlock Fundamentals & Prevention
slides.prompt: A deadlock occurs when two or more threads are blocked forever, each waiting for a resource held by another. Standard deadlock conditions include Mutual Exclusion, Hold & Wait, No Preemption, and Circular Wait.

slides.title: std::lock Function

std::mutex m1, m2;
std::___(m1, m2); // Deadlock-free locking algorithm

slides.title: Circular Wait Condition
slides.prompt: Which deadlock prevention strategy breaks the 'Circular Wait' condition?
options: Enforcing a global lock acquisition hierarchy order for all mutexes
Disabling exception handling in critical sections
Increasing the number of worker threads
slides.correctAnswer: Enforcing a global lock acquisition hierarchy order for all mutexes

slides.title: Livelock Description
slides.prompt: Fill in the term for a situation where threads continuously change state in response to each other without making progress.
slides.codeSnippet: // Threads are actively running but unable to progress = ___lock

slides.title: Thread Starvation Cause
slides.prompt: What causes thread starvation in concurrent systems?
options: A thread is perpetually denied necessary CPU or lock resources due to unfair scheduling or greedy priorities
A thread accesses invalid unmapped memory addresses
A mutex is unlocked out of order
Atomic operations consume all CPU cache bandwidth
slides.correctAnswer: A thread is perpetually denied necessary CPU or lock resources due to unfair scheduling or greedy priorities

slides.title: Spinlock Mechanism
slides.prompt: Fill in the term for a lock mechanism where a thread repeatedly polls in a busy loop until the lock becomes available.

slides.title: False Sharing Explanation
slides.prompt: What is false sharing in high-performance multithreaded applications?
options: Two threads on different CPU cores modify independent variables located on the exact same CPU cache line, causing cache invalidation traffic
Two threads read from separate dynamic libraries
Multiple processes map to identical virtual addresses
A lock guard incorrectly references a local mutex variable
slides.correctAnswer: Two threads on different CPU cores modify independent variables located on the exact same CPU cache line, causing cache invalidation traffic
